meta.title: Paradox Localization Translator — translate Paradox game mods with AI
meta.description: Free, unofficial tool to translate Crusader Kings III, Victoria 3, Hearts of Iron IV, Stellaris and Europa Universalis mods into 11 languages using a local LLM or a cloud AI.

suggest: This page is also available in English.

hero.title: Translate mods into **your language** — with a local LLM or a cloud AI.
hero.lead: A free desktop tool for modders and players. It translates mod localisation files for Crusader Kings III, Victoria 3, Hearts of Iron IV, Stellaris, Europa Universalis IV and V, and Imperator: Rome into any of the 11 languages the games support, keeps the game's formatting codes intact, and helps you find and fix what is still untranslated.
hero.platforms: Windows · macOS · Linux — no Python needed
hero.demo_caption: Formatting codes stay exactly as they were.

items.title: Translate whole mods at once
items.text: Add a single file, a localisation folder or an entire mod — or drag and drop it. Queue several mods; pause, resume, or stop and continue next time.

items.title: Keeps game code safe
items.text: Formatting codes such as `[ROOT.Char.GetName]`, `$VALUE$`, `£gold£` and `§Y…§!` are protected during translation and restored afterwards, so the game text does not break.

items.title: Repair and update, not just translate
items.text: Finds lines that were left untranslated and translates only those. Each job keeps its own cache: when a mod updates, lines that were already translated are reused, so only new or changed lines go to the AI.

items.title: Finds existing translation mods (Japanese)
items.text: For Japanese, it checks whether another mod already translates a mod, and whether that translation is complete. Missing lines can be added to the translation mod instead of the original — with a backup and a confirmation first.

items.title: Check and polish
items.text: Compare source and translation side by side, run quality checks, search and fix any line directly, and keep a glossary for each language so names and terms stay consistent.

items.title: Your choice of AI
items.text: Run a local model with Ollama or LM Studio — free and private — or use OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini or any OpenAI-compatible API. API keys are never saved to settings, profiles or logs.

shots.title: Screenshots
shots.ui_note: The app's interface is currently in Japanese; an English UI is planned.

games.title: Games and languages
games.intro: The tool can translate into all 11 official languages. Each game only reads some of them; if you choose a language the game cannot display, the tool warns you before it starts. Automatic mod detection covers Crusader Kings III, Victoria 3, Hearts of Iron IV, Stellaris and Europa Universalis V; for Europa Universalis IV and Imperator: Rome, add the files or folders yourself.
games.legend: ✓ = the game can display this language

steps.title: Prepare an AI
steps.text: Start Ollama or LM Studio and load a model — or have an API key ready for a cloud service.

steps.title: Download and open the app
steps.text: Pick the file for your system from the latest release.

steps.title: Choose the model
steps.text: In “Model / Connection”, select the provider and the model.

steps.title: Add a mod and translate
steps.text: Add a file, folder or mod (drag and drop works), choose the target language, and press “Start translation”.

steps.title: Check, then apply
steps.text: Review the result in QA / Compare, then write the finished translation into the mod. A backup is made first.

needs.title: What you need
needs.local: Ollama or LM Studio, and a model that writes your target language well (for example Qwen or Gemma models).
needs.cloud: An API key for OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, or an OpenAI-compatible service. Usage is billed by that service, not by this tool.

publish.title: Publishing a translated mod
publish.intro: If you share a translation made with this tool on Steam Workshop or elsewhere, please:

items.title: Ask the original mod's author for permission.
items.text: This is the custom in the modding community, and Steam's terms require that you hold the rights to what you upload.

items.title: Publish it for free.
items.text: Paradox Interactive's User Agreement (Section 5) requires mods and other user-generated content to be free for everyone; they cannot be put behind a paywall. Accepting donations for your time is allowed.

items.title: Say that it is machine-translated,
items.text: if it is. It helps players decide.

donate.title: Support development
donate.text: Donations go through GitHub Sponsors and are received by VF Software Co., Ltd. They support the development time and costs of all of our work, including this tool. Every feature stays free for everyone, and donating does not unlock anything.

items.a: Yes. Every feature is free for everyone, under the MIT License. There is no paid version.

items.q: Does every feature work for every language?
items.a: Translation, repair of untranslated lines, QA, search and glossaries work for all 11 languages. Mod survey, translation-mod detection and linking, update-only translation, Chinese-based translation and automatic glossary building are Japanese only for now. Quality checks are simpler for other languages: Korean, Russian and Simplified Chinese are checked by script; between Latin-script languages, only lines identical to the source are flagged.

items.q: macOS says the app cannot be opened.
items.a: The app is not signed by Apple. Open System Settings → Privacy & Security and allow it to open.
The app is not code-signed. Download it only from the official GitHub Releases page, then choose “More info” → “Run anyway”.

items.q: Can I translate Steam Workshop mods directly?
items.a: Yes, but a Workshop update can overwrite your changes. The tool keeps backups; for important work, keep a copy of the translation.

items.q: How do I report a bug?
items.a: Open an issue on GitHub. If you can, attach the diagnostic ZIP from Settings → Collect diagnostic log, and describe the steps. The ZIP does not include your translations or API keys.
